claims.text: The initial material is a homogeneous high-entropy alloy without an engineered solid-lubricant phase.
Nano-scale WS2 particulates can be introduced during high-entropy-alloy synthesis with a uniform dispersion.
Sliding stresses will cause dispersed WS2 particulates to form a continuous or semi-continuous tribofilm at the contact interface.
WS2 particulates become exposed at the alloy surface during sliding.
The layered, low-shear structure of WS2 facilitates interlayer sliding.
WS2-mediated interlayer sliding reduces direct asperity contact.
WS2-mediated interlayer sliding reduces interfacial stresses.
Reduced asperity contact and interfacial stresses lower the coefficient of friction.
Reduced asperity contact and interfacial stresses lower the wear rate.
The WS2-containing alloy will have a lower coefficient of friction than the untreated alloy under identical test conditions.
The WS2-containing alloy will have a lower wear rate than the untreated alloy under identical test conditions.
The reductions in coefficient of friction and wear rate are estimated to be 20–30%.
The WS2 intervention should remain effective from near-ambient to elevated temperatures under moderate to high sliding loads.
Agglomeration of WS2 particulates may reduce the intervention's effectiveness.
Temperatures exceeding the thermal-stability limit of the alloy or WS2 may reduce the intervention's effectiveness.
Environments that aggressively oxidize WS2 may reduce the intervention's effectiveness.

contradictions.description: The predicted 20–30% improvement is explicitly presented as an uncertain estimate, but the falsification rule treats an improvement outside that range as an example of failure. An improvement greater than 30% could be statistically significant and favorable, so being outside the estimated range is not equivalent to showing no significant reduction.
